cast_dialogue.linea: Words have best friends, heroes. 'Do research', 'make progress', 'meet deadlines' — collocations are the couples of vocabulary.
I want to make progress in my career, so I've applied for a job at a photo agency.
At the restaurant we meet deadlines every day. It's stressful, but we gain experience.
I'm doing research for my next novel, so I spend mornings taking notes at the library.
Make an effort now, mis héroes, and you'll reach your goals. Earn your salary, but never stop learning.

inicio.definicion_pragmatica: Collocations are natural word partnerships: we DO research, MAKE progress, MEET deadlines, EARN a salary, APPLY FOR a job, GAIN experience, REACH goals. Wrong partners sound strange: ❌ 'do progress', ❌ 'make research'.

reading.texto: Sofía is doing research for her next novel, so she spends mornings taking notes at the library. Ben wants to make progress in his career, so he has applied for a job at a photo agency. Kenji works hard to meet deadlines at the restaurant, while Abuela Carmen says young people should gain experience before they earn a high salary. They all agree: make an effort now, and you'll reach your goals.
